question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Masulipatnam — Location & Initial Factories]
options: Masulipatnam (Machilipatnam) is located on the Coromandel Coast of Andhra Pradesh, on the Bay of Bengal
The Dutch established their first factory in India at Masulipatnam in 1605
The English established their first factory on the east coast of India at Masulipatnam in 1611
Masulipatnam is located at the mouth of the Narmada River on the Arabian Sea coast
wrong_fact: Masulipatnam is NOT located at the mouth of the Narmada River on the Arabian Sea. It is located on the eastern coast of India (Andhra Pradesh) at the mouth of the Krishna River branch on the Bay of Bengal. The Narmada empties into the Arabian Sea on the western coast.
explanation: Masulipatnam (modern Machilipatnam) is situated on the Krishna River delta on the Bay of Bengal (Coromandel Coast). It was a major port for the Golconda Kingdom. The Dutch (1605) and English (1611) established their early trading factories here due to its proximity to Golconda's textile-producing hinterlands.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Masulipatnam — Golden Farman & Hinterland Trade]
options: In 1632, the Sultan of Golconda issued the Golden Farman, allowing the English to trade freely at Masulipatnam for a fixed duty
Masulipatnam was highly valued for its exports of fine painted and printed cotton cloth, known as chintz or kalamkari
The port of Masulipatnam declined in the late 17th century as EIC trade shifted to Fort St. George in Madras
The Golden Farman was issued by the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb after the annexation of Golconda
wrong_fact: The Golden Farman was NOT issued by the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb. It was issued in 1632 by Abdullah Qutb Shah, the Qutb Shahi Sultan of Golconda, who ruled the region. Aurangzeb did not annex Golconda until 1687.
explanation: The Qutb Shahi Sultan of Golconda issued the Golden Farman in 1632, allowing the English East India Company to trade freely from the kingdom's ports, including Masulipatnam, in exchange for a yearly payment of 500 pagodas. Masulipatnam was famous for Kalamkari textiles. As the English developed Madras (Fort St. George), trade shifted south, and Masulipatnam declined.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Masulipatnam — Carnatic Wars & Concession]
options: During the Seven Years' War, British forces under Colonel Francis Forde captured Masulipatnam from the French in 1759
Following the capture of Masulipatnam, Salabat Jung (Nizam of Hyderabad) signed a treaty ceding the Northern Circars (including Masulipatnam) to the British
Masulipatnam was captured by the French under Marquis de Bussy in 1750, who turned it into a major French stronghold on the East Coast
The Dutch ceded Masulipatnam to the British in 1688 after the Glorious Revolution unified the British and Dutch crowns under William of Orange
wrong_fact: The Dutch did NOT cede Masulipatnam to the British in 1688. Although William of Orange became King of England in the Glorious Revolution, the Dutch East India Company (VOC) and English East India Company (EIC) remained separate, competing corporate entities. The Dutch retained their factory at Masulipatnam until the late 18th century/early 19th century, when all Dutch possessions in India were formally transferred to Britain under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824.
explanation: In 1759, British officer Francis Forde led the Siege of Masulipatnam, successfully storming the French-controlled fort. The Nizam of Hyderabad, Salabat Jung, subsequently signed a treaty ceding Masulipatnam and the surrounding Northern Circars territory to the EIC. The French had earlier seized the town under Bussy in 1750. The Glorious Revolution did not merge the EIC and VOC, nor did the Dutch cede Masulipatnam in 1688.
